steps.bob_prompt: The contributing guide says the simplest way to set up a development environment for this project is to use tox. Locate the tox configuration in this repository that this instruction refers to, and confirm it is present.

check.describes: the tox configuration the instruction depends on

steps.quote: The simplest way to set up a development environment is to use [`tox`](https://tox.wiki/en/latest/installation.html).
steps.title: Use tox to set up the development environment

steps.bob_prompt: The guide states a minimum supported Python version. Determine what it is, then confirm the Python available in this environment satisfies it.

check.describes: the interpreter meets the documented minimum

steps.quote: **IMPORTANT:** Python 3.10 is the minimum version we support. Feel free to test on anything between `python3.10` and `python3.14`.
steps.title: Confirm the minimum supported Python version

steps.bob_prompt: The guide tells a new contributor to build and activate a virtual environment using the tox environment named dbt180. Confirm that tox environment is actually available in this repository.

check.describes: the dbt180 tox environment, via its brace expansion in envlist

steps.title: Build the virtual environment with the dbt180 tox env

steps.bob_prompt: The guide says the development environment installs an example plugin from a path inside this repository. Find that plugin directory and confirm it exists.

check.describes: the example plugin the environment installs

steps.quote: This virtual environment will already have the package installed in editable mode for you, as well as `requirements_dev.txt` and `plugins/sqlfluff-plugin-example`.
steps.title: Install the example plugin in editable mode

steps.bob_prompt: The guide gives a targeted tox invocation for day-to-day work naming four environments. Confirm the linting environment among them is defined in this repository.
steps.title: Run a targeted tox environment

steps.bob_prompt: For dialect work the guide says you can regenerate parse fixtures by running a script directly, and gives its path. Confirm that script is present.

check.describes: the fixture generation script named in the guide

steps.quote: `python test/generate_parse_fixture_yml.py -d mysql` will do the same.
steps.title: Regenerate the parse fixtures

steps.bob_prompt: The guide says that after changing a dialect you must resync the Rust dialects by running a script at a given path. Confirm that script exists.

check.describes: the rustify script named in the guide

steps.quote: with sqlfluff installed in a virtual environment, run `utils/rustify.py build` to resync the languages.
steps.title: Resync the Rust dialects

steps.bob_prompt: The guide says that if your change is to the AnyOf() grammar, you should first run the grammar test file it names. Locate that test file and run it.
steps.quote: 1. If your change is to the `AnyOf()` grammar, first running `tox -e py310 -- test/core/parser/grammar_test.py` would be wise.
steps.title: Run the grammar tests for an AnyOf() change

steps.bob_prompt: When developing an isolated rule, the guide says to run the yaml test cases file it names, filtered to one rule. Confirm that test file is present.
steps.title: Run the yaml rule test cases

steps.bob_prompt: The guide says the dbt templater tests need a local Postgres instance and that the connection parameters are in a profiles.yml at a specific path. Open that file and report the connection parameters.
steps.quote: The dbt templater tests require a locally running Postgres instance. See the required connection parameters in `plugins/sqlfluff-templater-dbt/test/fixtures/dbt/profiles.yml`.
steps.title: Find the dbt connection parameters

steps.bob_prompt: The guide gives an explicit tox command for running the dbt-related tests. Confirm every tox environment it names is available in this repository.

check.describes: a tox environment named dbt019, in tox.ini

steps.title: Run the dbt templater tests

steps.bob_prompt: The guide offers pre-commit hooks installed through a named tox environment. Confirm that environment is defined.
steps.title: Install the pre-commit hooks

steps.bob_prompt: The guide links to a separate README for building and testing the documentation website. Open it and confirm it is there.

check.describes: the documentation README the guide links to

steps.quote: See the [Documentation Website README.md](./docs/README.md) file for more information on how to build and test this.
steps.title: Read the documentation website guide

steps.bob_prompt: The release checklist says to store a GitHub personal access token in an environment variable with a specific name, then run the release script. Confirm the release script actually reads a variable with that name.
steps.quote: Once generated, store it in your env (zshrc, etc) as `SQLFLUFF_GITHUB_TOKEN`.
steps.title: Store the release token for the release script
